title: Pediatric arch support: final design review
coords: x and y are percent of the page image, measured from the top left
intro: Our 8 August 2026 design review. Start with the requirements on page 5 and the V2 sleeve on pages 7 and 8.

hotspots.title: Objective and need
hotspots.note: We aimed to reduce arch discomfort with an adjustable, low-cost sleeve. These were design goals.

hotspots.title: The Valmassy formula
hotspots.note: The slide cites RCSP = 7 minus age as a background rule of thumb. We did not measure heel angle.

hotspots.title: Benchmark table
hotspots.note: Rigid orthotics, store insoles and our sleeve rated on four rows. The sleeve column is design intent; none of it was tested.

hotspots.title: Needs turned into inputs
hotspots.note: The table sets targets of 10% growth, 150 N load and thickness under 8 mm, with planned verification methods. The reports provide no results for those checks.

hotspots.title: Why muslin and gel
hotspots.note: We chose muslin for the sewn sleeve and gel pads for the arch insert. Comfort and ease of use remained design goals.

hotspots.title: V1: cardboard and foam
hotspots.note: Cardboard and foam in standard socks. In the slide's words: verified the lift, failed on stability.

hotspots.title: V2: gel pads in sleeves
hotspots.note: V2 used gel pads in compression sleeves. It was steadier than V1; the next version needed a dedicated pad pocket.

hotspots.title: V3 proposal
hotspots.note: The proposed V3 used custom-molded hybrid inserts and a reinforced pouch. It was not built.

hotspots.title: The cut pattern
hotspots.note: Paper patterns for the bottom pad, top pad, pocket and back strap, with sewing steps: print on 8.5 by 11, cut the fabric, iron, sew the pocket, hand-sew it shut. This is how the prototype was made.

hotspots.title: Windlass model
hotspots.note: The arch modelled as a windlass: plantar fascia tension from ground reaction force, foot length and arch height. I helped with this analysis. The slide shows the formula, with no foot data run through it.

hotspots.title: Sleeve stress estimate
hotspots.note: Stress equals modulus times strain, with a modulus of 10 to 100 MPa 'based on stitch vs cross stretch'. It is a calculated range; we ran no tensile test on our fabric.

hotspots.title: Risk analysis
hotspots.note: The table lists five failure modes and proposed mitigations, including a reinforced gel casing.

hotspots.title: How we tested
hotspots.note: A 30 lb dumbbell sat on the insert for 1 minute, then was dropped on it from 1 foot. The test ran three static holds and three drops.

hotspots.title: What counts as a pass
hotspots.note: The insert has to stay fully intact: no gel outside the pouch, no stitching undone, no fabric torn.

hotspots.title: A frame from the bench test in our report
hotspots.note: A low-resolution still of the test, with the dumbbell on the ground. It shows the setup. No force was recorded.

hotspots.title: Gel containment
hotspots.note: The next sleeve needed better gel containment and a check on fabric tension against the foot.

hotspots.title: Future improvements
hotspots.note: TPU printed encasement and scan-to-print are listed as ideas. None was printed or built.
